rival_construction_interface.named_component_candidate: Define a stable object/reference from a caption and pay a later consumer that requires that same component identity, property or relation. Using only a generic site and an action without such object duty does not demonstrate the named-component construction.
rival_construction_interface.procedure_heading_candidate: Define an event/instruction or deictic procedure at a caption site and pay its participants and scope in a complete prose consumer. Reusing the caption as an opaque object ID does not demonstrate the procedural construction.
rival_construction_interface.possible_decision_changing_consequence: One fixed written consumer may require persistent component identity or may require a specific caption-introduced event/result. If those consequences cannot be mutually renamed while all written duties remain paid, the constructions differ. The image contract can check declared site/geometry duties, but cannot choose lexical kinds by itself.
rival_construction_interface.important_ceiling: A static component and an action performed at it can coexist. Both full readings fittingC83 is not a content winner. A current procedure word need not depict the action in the picture; a component name need not be nominally isolated in every usage.
